sentences.text: Shantungosuchus is an extinct crocodyliform genus belonging to the class Reptilia, known from fossils found in China.
The type species, S. chuhsienensis, was originally described from an articulated skeleton preserved as a ventral impression measuring approximately 30 cm in total length.

The genus was first described by Yang in 1961, and its name derives from Shandong, the Chinese province where the animal was first discovered, with the suffix 'suchus' referring to the Ancient Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile deity Sobek.
The genus includes three species: S. chuhsienensis and S. brachycephalus described by Yang Zhongjian in 1961 and 1982, and S. hangjinensis described by Xiao-Chun Wu et al. in 1994.

The group Protosuchia is now considered a paraphyletic grouping of early crocodyliforms, commonly divided into the basal family Protosuchidae and a group of basal crocodyliforms related to Hsisosuchus and Mesoeucrocodylia.

Research by Clark et al. (2004) and Buscalioni (2017) places Shantungosuchus in the superfamily Shartegosuchoidea, grouping it with Sichuanosuchus and Shartegosuchidae, confirming its membership in the parent group Shartegosuchoidea.

The genus lived between 143.1 and 125.77 million years ago, from the Berriasian to the Hauterivian stages, with S. chuhsienensis living during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Aptian) in the Mengyin Formation of Shandong province.

S. hangjinensis lived in the lower Cretaceous Luohandong Formation of Outer Mongolia, while S. brachycephalus may also have lived in that region, where fossils suggest it shared its habitat with fish like Sinamia, the turtle Ordosemys, the crocodyliform Ikechosaurus, and various unidentified dinosaurs.

There is an ongoing debate regarding the classification of Shantungosuchus, with some authors suggesting it is an atoposaurid while others, like Xiao-Chun Wu, argue it belongs to the family Protosuchidae.
